props.title: Synthetic-methanol process

props.name: any catalyst suitable for synthetic methanol production (mixtures of metallic oxides)

evidence.quote: In general, any 105 catalyst suitable for synthetic methanol pro- ) duction may be employed in the process, these catalysts ordinarily consisting of mixtures of metallic oxides
My process is in no way dependent on the use of a specific catalyst.

props.name: patent claim 1

evidence.quote: the step of removing said impurities from the gases by scrubbing them with liquid meth-

props.statement: In methanol manufacture from hydrogen and carbon oxides containing traces of impurities, over a catalyst at elevated pressure and temperature, the step of removing the impurities by scrubbing the gases with liquid methanol.

props.name: patent claim 2

evidence.quote: the step of combining the gases remaining unreacted, after a passage thereof in contact with the catalyst, with fresh gas, and removing impurities from the mixed gases by scrubbing them with liquid meth-

props.statement: In methanol manufacture, the step of combining unreacted gases after passage over the catalyst with fresh gas, and removing impurities from the mixed gases by scrubbing with liquid methanol.

props.name: patent claim 3

evidence.quote: scrubbing said incoming gases with the formed methanol during its removal from the process.

props.statement: In methanol manufacture from impure hydrogen and carbon oxides, removing the impurities by scrubbing the incoming gases with the formed methanol during its removal from the process.

props.name: patent claim 4

evidence.quote: the steps which comprise passing the gases in contact with liquid methanol under pressure,

props.statement: In synthetic methanol production at elevated pressure, passing the gases through liquid methanol under pressure, heating them by thermal contact with the hot reaction gases, contacting them with heated catalyst, cooling the reacted gases and removing the methanol, combining the residual gas with fresh gas and repeating the cycle.

props.name: impurities poison catalysts or cause side reactions

evidence.quote: While various imert gases such as methane and nitrogen are ordinarily regarded as non- - injurious, and hence tolerable by the reaction,
it is well known that very small amounts of certain other substances are poisonous to the catalysts employed, or may catalyze various. undesirable side reactions.
Among these undesirable impurities are in- cluded the, following :—volatile carbonyls of nickel and iron which may be formed by the ‘interaction of the hot carbon oxides with the apparatus;
gaseous mixture; and volatile sulfur and ar- senic compounds.

props.statement: While inert gases such as methane and nitrogen are ordinarily regarded as non-injurious, very small amounts of certain other substances poison the catalysts or catalyze undesirable side reactions: volatile carbonyls of nickel and iron formed from hot carbon oxides and the apparatus, oil vapors from the compressors, water vapor in the recirculated gas, amino compounds, and volatile sulfur and arsenic compounds.

props.name: origins of impurities and build-up on recirculation

evidence.quote: They may be present in the - gaseous mixture entering the reaction; they . may be formed by the reaction; or they may be formed by the gradual decomposition. of the apparatusemployed.
Even if a.gas mixture of extremely high purity is initially supplied to the process, im- | purities are built up in the manner described,

props.statement: Impurities may be present in the entering gas, formed by the reaction, or formed by gradual decomposition of the apparatus; even with a gas of extremely high initial purity, impurities build up during recirculation of the gases.

props.note: stated by the patent as well known
props.statement: Mixtures of hydrogen and carbon oxides (carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide or mixtures), hydrogen preferably in volumetric excess, react to form methanol when passed over heated catalysts at pressures in excess of 50 atmospheres and temperatures in excess of 280 °C.

props.name: scrubbing with liquid methanol removes poisons

evidence.quote: I have now discovered that the injurious substances present or formed in the gas mix- | ture employed for the methanol synthesis may 6¢ be removed in a simple fashion by merely “scrubbing” the gases with liquid methanol.
simply bubbled through or “scrubbed” with liquid methanol under elevated pressure, the undesirable substances constituting catalyst. poisons, etc., are dissolved in the methanol.
This method of purification is extremely ad- vantageous since it does not require the use of extra chemicals or of heat,

props.statement: Injurious substances present or formed in the synthesis gas may be removed by scrubbing the gases with liquid methanol under elevated pressure; the catalyst poisons dissolve in the methanol. No extra chemicals or heat are needed, it runs at the synthesis pressure, and since only the product methanol is used the gas cannot be contaminated with foreign substances.

props.name: intermittent or continuous scrubber operation

evidence.quote: the liquid circulat- ing pump may be operated either intermit- x» tently or continuously.
The scrubber may then be filled with Raschig rings or similar tower packing material,

props.statement: The liquid circulating pump may be run intermittently (scrubber filled with methanol, product drained from the receiver, scrubber methanol periodically replaced) or continuously (all product methanol passes through the scrubber and leaves by its drain); in continuous operation the methanol level may be lowered and the scrubber filled with Raschig rings or similar packing over which the methanol is sprayed.

props.name: purifier mass filters gas and decomposes carbonyls

evidence.quote: consist of copper turnings or asbestos fiber, or, indeed, of some of the catalyst employed in the reaction.
Its function 1s to act as a sort of gas filter and to decompose any traces of metallic carbonyls which might otherwise ,,,
the use of a purifier mass is no longer absolutely necessary.

props.statement: The purifier mass may consist of copper turnings, asbestos fiber or some of the catalyst; it acts as a gas filter and decomposes traces of metallic carbonyls that might otherwise reach the catalyst. With methanol scrubbing it is no longer absolutely necessary, but it is preferably kept as an additional safeguard.

props.name: scrubbing methanol stays marketable

evidence.quote: the use — of some of the methanol formed in the process © as the purification medium does not render it “impure” under ordinary industrial stand-

props.statement: Because the impurities are small in amount, the product methanol used for scrubbing is not rendered impure under ordinary industrial standards and may be marketed without treatment to remove the dissolved impurities.
